property_summary: Only the owner is allowed to successfully call withdrawAll (i.e., calls by non-owners always revert).
If a call to withdrawAll succeeds (does not revert) then the caller must be the owner.

If withdrawAll succeeds then the recipient is not the owner implies the caller must be the owner (i.e., non-owner callers can only succeed when sending funds to themselves), ensuring non-owners cannot withdraw funds to other addresses.
If the call to withdrawAll did not revert and the recipient is not the owner, then the caller must be the owner.

For all inputs, only the owner may successfully withdraw the contract balance via withdrawAll(recipient) (i.e., non-owners cannot make the contract transfer funds away); the mutant that allows recipient==owner relaxes this and lets a non-owner trigger a transfer to the owner, violating the rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any recipient, only the owner address passed at construction can cause the contract to transfer out its balance when calling withdrawAll(recipient); the mutant that allows withdraw when recipient==owner permits a non-owner caller to trigger transfer to the owner, violating this rule for some inputs.

For every caller and recipient, only a call from the contract owner can cause the contract balance to be drained by withdrawAll; the mutant that also allows calls when recipient==owner lets a non-owner caller (with recipient equal to owner) drain the balance, violating this rule for some inputs.

For all callers and recipients, if a non-owner calls withdrawAll the contract balance must remain unchanged (only the owner may cause the contract balance to become zero); the mutant permitting withdraw when recipient==owner allows a non-owner to drain the balance when they pass the owner as recipient, violating this rule for some fuzzed inputs.
